reasoning:
Range-construction lens: hero's POST-PREFLOP range as UTG cold-caller of CO 3-bet in 4-way pot is tightly capped. UTG cold-calls a 3-bet with: AA/KK (slowplay subset — most AA/KK 4-bet, but a fraction cold-call to balance), QQ-JJ (mostly call), TT-77 (call), AQs (mostly call, sometimes 4-bet), AJs/KQs/KJs (some), small suited connectors (rare). UTG does NOT have AK, AQ, broadway off-suit, sub-9 pairs. The cold-call range is roughly 30-40 combos, narrow.

On QhJh3s:
  - SETS: QQ (3 combos) = 1 (1 Q on board so QQ has 3 combos still wait Q is on board, so QQ combos = C(3,2) = 3; JJ similarly = 3; 33 = 3). Hero's range includes QQ, JJ for sets — 6 combos top set+second set.
  - TWO PAIR: QJ — but hero's range has KJs maybe but not QJ at cold-call frequency, ~0 combos.
  - OVERPAIRS: AA (3 combos slowplay subset → ~1 combo at this node weight), KK (3 combos × slowplay weight ~1).
  - TPGK/TPTK: KQs (3 combos × call weight), AQs (some — 3 combos × call weight ~2).
  - SECOND PAIR: AJs/KJs (suited Jx).
  - FDs: KhXh suited combos (1-2), JhTh (1) — minimal nut FD density.
  - MARGINAL: TT, 99, 88, 77 — 6 combos × 4 = 24 combos but each ~2 combos by suit.

Hero range density on QhJh3s favors MEDIUM-STRENGTH (overpairs and second pair). Hero's range NUTTED density is concentrated in QQ/JJ/AA/KK (~10 combos). The CO 3-bettor's range NUTTED density is QQ/AK with FD (5-6 combos plus JJ which CO usually has). CO's range is more polar; hero's range is more medium.

Range-vs-range, hero on QhJh3s is BEHIND CO on nutted-equity but AHEAD on polar-bluff equity. Hero CANNOT lead-bet large on the medium-strength bucket without becoming face-up: a 66% lead from UTG cold-caller polarizes hero's range. CO can attack 66%-lead by jam-or-fold with KK/QQ/JJ-block hands.

Furthermore: the donk-lead protocol from a cold-caller in 3-bet pot multiway is essentially uninvented in modern solver outputs. Solvers do explore small (25-33%) range-lead from cold-callers on boards where the cold-caller has a CLEAR range advantage (low rainbow boards like 5-4-2 where CO 3-bettor's range is mostly overcards). QhJh3s is NOT that board — CO has Q/J in his range; hero does not have a structural advantage.

For AhAs specifically: the Ah-blocker AGAINST the heart-FD has two effects:
  (+) Reduces villains' implied odds — they can't make the nut flush.
  (-) Reduces protection EV — fewer villain combos have FD to deny.
  (-) Removes hero's own FD-pickup — hero already holds a heart; the rest are out.
Net: the BLOCKER REDUCES BET FREQUENCY for AhAs vs no-Ah AA combos (AdAs/AdAc/AsAc/AcAd — but AA combos are only AhAs, AhAc, AhAd, AsAc, AsAd, AcAd). Of 6 AA combos, 3 hold Ah, 3 don't. The 3 NON-Ah combos (AsAc, AsAd, AcAd) want to BET more because they don't block the FD they want to deny. AhAs WANTS TO CHECK MORE because the Ah blocker doubles as range-cap-disguise + reduces protection target.

The consensus rationales misread this: they treated Ah as a 'nut-FD blocker that BOOSTS betting' (protection logic) when in fact for hero's specific node (cold-caller OOP multiway 3bet pot), the Ah-blocker is a CHECK-leverage card (slowplay the nut FD blocker, induce protection bets from CO's no-FD overpairs, raise turn).

Verdict: CHECK at MEDIUM-HIGH confidence. The class-level AA frequency on this node is high-CHECK (~85%); the AhAs combo specifically lands at the LOW end of the bet frequency (~12%) due to the Ah-blocker REDUCING protection EV. The consensus mass-vote BET 66% inverts the correct blocker reasoning. Sizing 66% would be wrong even if BET were chosen — small range-lead protection sizing 25-33% would be the only defensible bet sizing in multiway 3bet pot OOP.

Class-vs-combo decomposition for AA on this node: of 6 AA combos × 15% class BET freq = 0.9 combos of BET weight. The 3 no-Ah AA combos absorb the BET weight at ~25-30% each; the 3 Ah-bearing AA combos check at ~95%+. AhAs is in the high-check subset. LABEL: CHECK.
